APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF APRIL 2, 2019

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:02 pm

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Jerry Velasco, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Councilmember Ancona  5-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION (6:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).
   City Council Meeting Minutes of April 2, 2019

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
  deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
  agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
  Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
  Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
  instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
  of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
  proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
  public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
  of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
  threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
  interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
  must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
  religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
  marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

  Vanessa Rodriguez – Parks and Recreation Pee Wee Cheerleading.

  Steven Trumble – Representing L.A. County Libraries as always and I want to let you

   City Council Meeting Minutes of April 2, 2019

  Frank Chavez – I am a 45 year resident of the City of El Monte and I live with epilepsy
  and I have seizure disorder. I know there are two items regarding approval for cannabis
  for medicinal purposes. In favor of the project.

  Gabriel Ramirez – I have been getting the run around at City Hall regarding red curb. I
  have had consistent problems today, last week and the following weeks I have almost
  been in a car accident. I have had the Police Department and I have made a petition
  because we had a red curb for a reason. We have a neighbor that has a medical
  problem and there was an incident when the Fire Department and the ambulance
  couldn’t find parking there because it was blocked.

  Julio Ramirez – I haven’t been coming lately. I have been begging for almost nine years
  to have a union store right here. I see my Teamster s brothers right here and I see two
  Councilmembers supported by the union and we haven’t had a union shop right here.
  We have been denied. We have been denied on the movie theater, baseball fields.
  Let’s get our act together we need a store union.

  Jane Myring – I am here on a happier note on April 27th the El Monte Women’s Club is
  having a fashion show it is called “Going for the Roses”. We are asking the ladies to
  wear big hats we are going to kind of celebrate a week before the Kentucky Durby time
  but we thought it would be so fun. We are inviting everybody it is $30 for the lunch and
  the fashion show by Magnolias in Arcadia and they have wonderful fashions. It will be on
  April 27th at the Grace T. Black Auditorium beginning at 10:30 am and we will probably
  go until 2:00 pm. We invite everyone to come to our meetings they are the 4th Thursday
  of the month at 11:00 am.

  Maryann Powers – Good evening and Happy New Year. I follow both the Police
  Department and our Chief on Facebook and I see so many of our officers involved with
  the children of this community and I think it is time to say thank you to them. The other
  thing I want to mention is that Norms comes to the City and we say that they have to hire
  residents of El Monte for their jobs. Now we are saying the same thing about the
  cannabis industry. We have said that about some of the auto dealerships. How about
  the City, how many of the last jobs have gone to residents of this community? I find it
  absolutely fascinating that Public Works needs another Assistant Director and I am
  hearing the same thing about Parks and Recreation but we are losing employees. What
  is the ratio of supervisor to employee in those departments? I think it is time that we
  really take a look at this. Do you think that the residents of our City are only good to be
  waiters or dishwashers or watering marijuana plants or maybe washing cars at the local
  dealership. I think some of those jobs should

  Lui Ma – Tonight as a resident I had to voice my concern for our City and our Nation.
  We may up rise by our Constitutional right and freedom of speech. However, if this
  freedom of speech is abused against a particular person that would be called slander
  and also if any organization conduct illegal ways to achieve a goal including to use
  children as a weapon that is not right. On March 27th the Chinese version of the World
  Journal published an article on page 3 and I received written permission from the World
  Journal and I will now submit it as a public record.

12.  CONSENT CALENDAR:

  All matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine in nature and
  may be enacted by one motion approving the recommendation listed on the Agenda.
  One or more items may be removed from the Consent Calendar so that they may be

  quorum.

  12.1  Approval for Second Reading of an Uncodified Ordinance Approving: (1)

  Cultivation, Manufacturing, and Distribution of Medicinal Cannabis at 4377
  Baldwin Avenue, El Monte, California; and (2) a Notice of Exemption for Such
  Project.
  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Ratify the proposed Ordinance by second reading by at least three (3)
  affirmative votes.

  Total Cost: N/A  Account No: N/A
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

  Ordinance No. 2945

  Carrie Chen – I strongly oppose the City Council’s decision to approve the first
  commercial cultivation plan. My objection is based on the following reasons: El
  Monte officials have abused their discretion under CEQA; secondly, the Notice of

  6
   City Council Meeting Minutes of April 2, 2019

Exemption itself is defective as an information disclosure document. I strongly
oppose to the adoption of these two ordinances.

Ron Williams – Here we are again talking about marijuana I don’t know why we
are discussing marijuana. I see that the Teamsters are here in full force I
recognize that they have an interest and a financial benefit.

Frank Angel – I refer to our written submittals from March 19th and our written
submittals from today because the vote will be 4-1 so no matter what we are
saying it is not going to make a difference.

Ellis Raskin – As you have been told before the CEQA review for these projects
is substantially defective in many ways. There is no mention at all of the at least
eight (8) other projects that have been proposed within the two block area
bordering these. We know about the last two others that have been approved
within the last few months. There is no consideration of the cumulative impacts.
There are no disclosures of impacts on public services. We urge you tonight to
do the right thing.

Fenglan Liu – Before I speak I submit written statements regarding 12.1 and
12.2. I am here speaking on behalf of Greater SGV Safe Community
Foundation. Personally I want to talk about CEQA 15332 the Class 332
Exemption of projects are illegal. The class 332 only apply to urban area these
two projects are in the industrial area so this waiver is illegal. Second I want to
rate the water quality from your City records. According to the 2015 Urban Water
Management Plan prepared by the City’s Water Department the City anticipates
to not have enough water.

Tom Meng – Against the project.

Diane Cheung – I am here to tell you to say no to marijuana projects in your City
because it is not good it is bad. We do not support not legal marijuana.

Sam Meng – I am here in front of you regarding 12.1 and 12.2 and I want to say
again what I said last time that there is no disclosure or we do not know for sure
what these factories are making. Hopefully the community can deserve for
themselves what these two chemicals are and what they do to the body and as
we have seen from articles that THC is dangerous. There are already a lot of
reports that show that THC are more harmful than dangerous.

Kewui Zhau – I would like to vote no to these two projects that you are
considering for the following reasons: the commercial marijuana cultivation and
production here is disguised as medicinal use because medicinal use has a very
strict meaning and regulations; and also marijuana growers target recreational
market rather than actual pharmaceutical companies for the downstream
process. Also the project can cause harm to children and teenagers in
surrounding areas. So I ask members to vote no to both projects.

Lui Ma – I support both projects 12.1 and 12.2 because they are legal highly
regulated. Mayor I written inquiry to the State Bar of California and I submit for
public records. If any attorney licensed lawyer in California use political language

  7
   City Council Meeting Minutes of April 2, 2019

  like recall against you can file a complaint with the State Bar and if the lawyer is
  also registered in Chinese government you can file a report to the People of the
  Republic of China, Justice Department, Attorney General. I support both projects
  please vote yes.

  Lou Villalvazo – Secretary/Treasurer with Teamsters Local 630 in Los Angeles.
  The number one question is why are we here and the bottom line is we want
  people to stop putting fear ahead of regulated patient access to medicinal
  cannabis. Prop 64 passed and it is the law of the land. All the constituents in the
  State of California passed 64. 30 States have passed initiatives to legalize
  cannabis. Clinical research has advanced since cannabis was approved. What
  you prefer manufactured drugs, opioids? You have millions of Americans who
  are hooked on pain killers opioids. This project is to decide whether or not to
  approve the cultivation, manufacturing, and distribution of medicinal cannabis.
  This is not a dispensary this will not have access to kids or even the public.
  Teamsters Local 630 here and our members who are here brought their families
  they are actual residents of this City. We ask that you approve this project as it
  will bring good jobs. It is going to provide for taxes and resources to the residents
  of El Monte. Teamsters Local 630 support good American jobs, manufacturing
  jobs especially when jobs are being shipped overseas specifically to China.

  18B.1 Discussion of Cinco De Mayo.

  12
   City Council Meeting Minutes of April 2, 2019

  I would like to request from my colleagues for the City to co-sponsor the
  event on May 4th. The event will be held after the Police Department 5K
  run and funding from that will be used along with potential programming
  funds from last year. No new funding is being requested that if there is it
  will be brought up and we will make sure that we will raise the funds. The
  event will be from 11:30 am to 5:30 pm at Arceo Park on May 4th.

18C.  Councilwoman Ancona

  I wanted to share that I attended the first Foothill Transit meeting as a board
  member and it was a great meeting loved their facilities. Along the lines of what
  Councilmember Martinez Muela said yes Duarte did launch their first line of
  electric buses. They launched three electric buses and services started
  yesterday. The City of Duarte is looking to converting their entire fleet of 35
  buses to zero emission buses so I know how we can get in on that so I will
  asking questions and lobbying for El Monte to get electric buses over here as
  well. The other thing that Foothill transit is looking at getting is double decker
  electric buses theses buses can hold up to 80 passengers. They’ve test driven
  some of these and they meet the height requirements and they can get through
  all the underpasses from here to Downtown LA. We also had Metrolink come in
  and give a presentation and they discussed what they do when there is some
  service interruption. It could take up to three hours so Metrolink explained their
  partnership with Foothill transit to get more buses out there. Metrolink also works
  with Uber and Lift to provide passengers with alternative needs to get to their
  destination.

18D.  Councilwoman Martinez Muela

  Come and support our young women at the cheer jamboree on Saturday doing
  what they do best and in cheering for their parks. This is just their beginning
  when they look back 20 years from now they are going to say I was a
  cheerleader. Today is all about children. We do have a couple of events coming
  up that are children related. First of all the PeeWee Jamboree coming up this
  Saturday and then next week we will be doing a Children’s Hospital Blood Drive.
  Children’s Hospital is dear to my heart it is a little different than the Red Cross.
  Children’s Hospital relies solely on your donations they don’t go to the Red Cross
  for donations. We will accept those members of the community coming in to
  donate blood and we hope to have a record year. So if you are interested of
  being a part of our blood drive please give a call to City Hall and we will make
  sure to put you in as an appointment. The Saturday after our Cheerleading
